subject: math
title: JC H2 functions and graphs: transformations, reciprocal functions, asymptote behaviour Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: Which statement about the graph of y = f(x + 3) is correct?

choices.text: It is y = f(x) shifted 3 units to the right
It is y = f(x) shifted 3 units to the left
It is y = f(x) shifted 3 units up

questions.misconception: f(x + 3) shifts the graph 3 units to the right.
questions.feedback: If you picked the first option, that is the trap: f(x + 3) shifts the graph 3 units to the right. Reteach point - root check: f(x + 3) = 0 at x = -3, and -3 sits to the left of the original root, so inside the brackets means shift LEFT.

questions.prompt: Describe fully the transformation that maps y = f(x) onto y = 2f(x) + 1.
questions.answer: A vertical stretch by a factor of 2, followed by a translation of 1 unit up.
questions.feedback: Both changes are outside f, so both act vertically: check you named the stretch factor 2 and the lift of 1 separately - if you described a horizontal change, the change you were reading was inside the brackets.

questions.prompt: What are the asymptotes of y = 1/x?
questions.feedback: The denominator is zero at x = 0, giving the vertical asymptote x = 0, and as x grows the values flatten onto the horizontal asymptote y = 0. The curve approaches both lines but never touches either.

questions.prompt: Rewrite f(3x + 3) in the form f(3(x + c)) and give the value of c.
questions.feedback: Factor out the 3 first: 3x + 3 = 3(x + 1). If you answered c = 3 you read the shift before factoring - the squeeze by 3 rescales the shift, which is why the factored form is the safe one to read.
